title: Actual affine finite-free resolution of a quasi-coherent complex
statement: Let U be an affine open subscheme of a scheme T [def-pc-scheme], C a complex of quasi-coherent O_U-modules [def-pc-derived-category], and d a natural number. Suppose C vanishes termwise above d and its complex of global sections is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then there exists a complex Q of O_U-modules vanishing above d, each of whose terms is finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and an actual quasi-isomorphism Q→C. No geometric morphism, nonnegative bound, or flatness hypothesis is required.

proof.text:
Exactness of global sections on quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme
identifies C with the associated sheaf complex of its global sections. Pseudo-coherence
and the vanishing above d give a bounded-above finite-free ring model with upper bound d
by Tag 064U. A bounded-above projective complex is K-projective; lift the derived
isomorphism into the global-sections complex to an actual chain map, whose cone is acyclic.
The exact tilde functor sends this map to a quasi-isomorphism. Compose with the affine
counit to obtain Q → C; tilde sends finite free modules to free sheaves of the same rank.
Zero complexes, including the empty base, give rank zero. No flatness is needed.
